knowledge_used.how_applied: Principles 1-5 and the six-step procedure applied: budget along the real path with this design's 50 degC ambient, 150/125 degC limits and 0.41 K/W R_thJC; shared-sink insulation; losses first; drivers under the device leads; NTC is not T_J. TI instance values (40 degC, 0.5 degC/W sink, 0.1 degC/W pad, 50/69 W limits) were not copied and were found not reproducible from the Ohmite/Wakefield datasheets.

Hard constraint evaluated: P_max = (T_J,lim - T_A)/(2*R_th,HS + R_pad + R_JC) = 38.9 W (150 degC) and 29.2 W (125 degC) against 28.7 W worst-case per device; required R_th,HS table derived for both limits.

Rated insulating pad selected (Sil-Pad TSP 3500, 4 kVac) with its resistance (0.63-0.82 K/W) in the budget; pad oversized for edge creepage; capacitance/displacement current added as an extra selection criterion; voltage rating and creepage surfaced for human review as the rule requires.

NTC on the earthed sink treated as cooling supervision; T_J mapping given as an estimate (T_NTC + 39-43 K at full load, load dependent); trip levels, calibration and the isolation route are surfaced for review, not decided.

Isolated thermistor path via a gate-driver AIN/APWM channel offered as the isolation option if the control ground is not PE-bonded; the chosen sensor is a ring-lug NTC on the PE-potential heatsink rather than a module NTC; calibration with a fixed resistor adopted.

Decision 9 model (two TO-247 per insulated forced-air sink) adopted; the factor 2 interpreted as shared-sink; TI's parts CR201-50VE and CD-02-05-247 evaluated as candidates and not selected (no forced-air data / 25-week lead; 76 um pad capacitance). Decision 10 driver placement reused.

Decision 8 rationale (NTC isolation can fail after a catastrophic event) considered; here the NTC sits on a protectively earthed sink, so the hazard differs; isolation decision passed to the architecture agent.
Copper sizing by an IPC-2221/2152-style temperature-rise estimate for 25/27.5 A on 70 um copper, repeated on two layers with via arrays.
Width, via count and loss rationale provided as the human-review evidence the rule asks for.
Creepage sink-to-tab and sink-to-HV copper estimated at 5.0 mm (500 V, PD2, group IIIa) and used to oversize the pads; the governing figure must be set by the isolation review.
Slots suggested around earthed heatsink mounting pins if surface creepage to HV copper is limiting.
Via SKILL-006 principle 4: gate drivers and decoupling on the opposite board side directly below the TO-247 leads so the sink placement does not lengthen gate or commutation loops.
Device pitch limited to 28 mm (pad-size driven) to keep the commutation loop short while meeting pad creepage.
Mechanical placement defined so the commutation loop overlay can still be minimised (devices adjacent on one sink face).
NTC and fan TACH wiring routed away from the switch node.
HV ceramics beside the legs are in the hottest PCB zone; a >= 125 degC rating requirement is handed to the capacitor agent.
Short-circuit protection timing is not a thermal-path item; only noted that OTP is a slow (seconds) protection and must not be relied on for device faults.

Both TO-247-4 on the sink's long face toward the half-bridge/HV-ceramic area at 28 mm pitch, lead row 3-5 mm from the face, bodies 20-25 mm above the PCB; footprint with Kelvin source per the MOSFET agent (KR-PCB-003).

Gate drivers, rail decoupling and gate resistors on the bottom side directly below the device leads so the sink placement does not lengthen gate or commutation loops (SKILL-006 principle 4; KR-PCB-005; KR-PCB-002; PE-PCB-001; KR-PCB-004; PE-PCB-003).

No HV copper (VIN+, SW, VOUT, DESAT nets) on outer layers within 5 mm of the heatsink outline, its clips and its earthed mounting pins; inner-layer HV pours under the sink only if the solid-insulation path is accepted by the isolation review; slots around mounting pins if surface creepage limits (KR-ISO-002, KR-ISO-004; 5.0 mm is an estimate for human review).
Heatsink bonded to protective earth through a dedicated PCB pad/wire on a PE net separate from PGND; the fan frame and NTC lug are at the same potential.

Pads are custom-cut Sil-Pad TSP 3500 28 x 32 mm (or one 60 x 32 mm strip), no mounting hole; clip metal must keep >= 3 mm clearance to the device leads; if screw mounting is chosen instead, use Boyd 7721-7PPSG shoulder washers with #4-40/M2.5 screws and die-cut pads with holes.

NTC (Vishay NTCALUG01A103F) mounting point: M3 thread-forming hole on the device face between the two TO-247 bodies, <= 10 mm from the HS tab; leads as a twisted pair to the control connector away from the switch node (PE-PCB-005), 2.2 kohm pull-up to 3.00 V and an RC filter at the ADC; add a hardware comparator output to an ePWM trip-zone input.
Fan connector (12 V, GND, TACH) at the fan end; fan supply current-limited; TACH to an eCAP/GPIO for stall detection.

Power nets carrying 25-27.5 A: >= 12 mm wide pours on 70 um outer layers (>= 22 mm on inner layers), repeated on two layers and stitched; >= 24 vias of 0.3 mm drill per 25 A layer transition (KR-PCB-006, PE-PCB-006).
Film DC-link and output capacitors >= 20 mm from the heatsink body and outside the exhaust; electrolytics (if any) >= 30 mm; HV ceramics beside the legs rated >= 125 degC (KR-CAP-003).
Inductor (60-80 mm envelope) placed laterally beside the sink in the fan bypass stream, >= 20 mm from the sink, >= 15 mm from the film capacitors, outside the exhaust cone.
Provide thermocouple test points: a flat spot on the sink beside each device and probe access to the device case edge (SKILL-006 verification step 6).

Partition compatibility: sink, devices, pads, clips, NTC and fan stay on the power board in every partition; only NTC and TACH signals cross to the control domain, through the barrier required by the architecture.
open_issues: All Fischer LAM 5 K 100 12 figures (0.68 K/W, airflow, fan current, mass, natural-convection resistance, meaning of the K suffix) are distributor-level because fischerelektronik.de blocked automated access; the datasheet must be obtained and the BOM confirmed before freeze.

The 125 degC preferred junction limit is met with typical parts (122.9 degC) but not with max-R_DS(on) parts (131.1 degC) on the single-width sink; decide between accepting this and adopting LAM 5 D K 100 12 (0.30 K/W, 100 mm wide, T_J 101-107 degC).
Interface resistance under clip pressure (0.80 K/W assumed) must be measured; if the case-to-sink drop exceeds about 1 K/W at 28.7 W, switch to screw mounting (0.63 K/W) or the upgrade sink.
Fan current (0.3 A placeholder) must be confirmed against the <= 2 A auxiliary 12 V budget (aux-supply agent).

Fan-failure survival depends entirely on the OTP: natural-convection resistance is an estimate, so the test plan needs a fan-stall test at reduced power with case thermocouples; a fan TACH fault should derate within 2 s.

Creepage from the earthed sink/clips to drain tabs and HV copper is set at 5.0 mm from memory of IEC 60664-1; the isolation/architecture agent must fix the governing standard and distances (KR-ISO-002) and confirm the 4 kVac pad rating is acceptable as basic insulation at 480 V peak (type-test voltage to be defined).

Pad capacitance drives 2-4 A displacement-current pulses into PE at each edge; the EMC design (CM choke, Y-capacitor strategy) must account for it, or the thicker 0.508 mm TSP 3500 / Al2O3 option taken at a 0.3-0.4 K/W thermal penalty.

NTC isolation route (direct ADC vs CB-PR-002 driver AIN vs digital isolator) depends on whether the SELV control ground is bonded to PE - architecture decision; KR-TH-003 calibration with a fixed resistor and a thermocouple-validated T_J estimator remain firmware-contract items.

Inductor (6-10 W) and film-capacitor hot-spot limits are placeholders until the inductor and capacitor agents report; a 60 mm inductor at 10 W cannot live in still air and may need a second fan or ducting.

Knowledge-base note: SKILL-006's TI instance values (CR201-50VE 0.5 degC/W, CD-02-05-247 0.1 degC/W) are not supported by the manufacturers' datasheets (3.3 K/W natural, 0.107 degC-in2/W); the skill should carry a caveat.
The 10 s overload is treated as steady state (conservative); transient and power-cycling lifetime are out of scope (SKILL-006 known limitation).

Fetched datasheets: Bergquist TSP 3500 and TSP A2000 (TDS Nov 2018), Wakefield ulTIMiFlux CD-02-05 (undated), Vishay NTCALUG01A (rev 17-Nov-17), Ohmite CR series (rev 2/18-1 via Farnell copy). markdown:
# Thermal design, heatsink, interface materials and mechanical envelopes

## 1. Inputs and loss re-check

Design basis: 50 degC ambient, forced air >= 2 m/s from a 12 V fan, junction design limit 150 degC (preferred 125 degC, device maximum 175 degC), both Wolfspeed C4MS025120K (TO-247-4, R_thJC 0.41 K/W) on one shared, protectively earthed heatsink with rated insulating pads (KR-TH-002; REF-TI-TIDA-010054 decision 9). Losses are the MOSFET agent's values at T_J = 150 degC and typical R_DS(on) 48.5 mohm; the max-R_DS(on) row scales conduction by 57.2/48.5.

| Corner (T_J 150 degC) | P_HS (W) | P_LS (W) | P_total (W) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 V / 25 A nominal | 25.1 | 21.6 | 46.7 |
| 440 V / 25 A | 24.6 | 23.3 | 47.9 |
| 440 V / 27.5 A (worst, typ R) | 28.7 | 27.5 | 56.2 |
| 440 V / 27.5 A, max R_DS(on) | 31.7 | 31.2 | 62.9 |

Conduction re-check (SKILL-006 principle 3): at 440 V / 27.5 A, D = 0.4545, dI = 8.17 A; I_rms,HS = sqrt(D*(Io^2 + dI^2/12)) = 18.61 A -> 18.61^2 * 0.0485 = 16.8 W; I_rms,LS = 20.38 A -> 20.2 W. Both match the MOSFET agent to 0.1 W.

## 2. Thermal model and required heatsink resistance

Shared-sink model (KR-TH-001; SKILL-006 principle 1): T_J,dev = T_A + P_total * R_th,HS + P_dev * (R_th,pad + R_th,JC). TI's unexplained factor 2 on the sink term (REF-TI-TIDA-010054 decision 9, EC-019/020) is read as two devices sharing one sink; with near-equal losses P_total * R_th,HS is the same statement. Required sink resistance: R_th,HS <= (T_J,lim - T_A - P_dev*(R_pad + R_JC)) / P_total.

| Case | R_pad (K/W) | R_th,HS for T_J <= 150 | R_th,HS for T_J <= 125 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typ R, P_HS 28.7 W, P_total 56.2 W | 0.80 (clip, ~25 psi) | 1.16 K/W | 0.72 K/W |
| typ R | 0.63 (screw, 50 psi) | 1.25 K/W | 0.80 K/W |
| max R, P_HS 31.7 W, P_total 62.9 W | 0.80 | 0.98 K/W | 0.58 K/W |
| max R | 0.63 | 1.07 K/W | 0.67 K/W |

A sink of about 0.7 K/W at the design airflow is therefore the target; 0.3 K/W would make the 125 degC preference hold even with max-R_DS(on) parts.

## 3. Heatsink selection

| Candidate | R_th forced (K/W) | R_th natural (K/W) | Size (mm) | Verification | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fischer LAM 5 K 100 12 (12 V fan integrated, clip variant) | 0.68 (RS listing for LAM 5 100 12) | not found (est. 3-4) | 100 x 50 x 50 | distributor listings only | SELECTED |
| Fischer LAM 5 D K 100 12 (double width) | 0.30 (distributor) | not found; sibling D K 125 24: 1.73 (DigiKey) | 100 x 100.5 x 50 | distributor | upgrade option |

Selected: Fischer Elektronik LAM 5 K 100 12 miniature cooling aggregate (50 x 50 mm hollow finned extrusion, 100 mm long, built-in 12 V axial fan, "K" = clip mounting per distributor descriptions). With R_th,HS = 0.68 K/W: T_sink = 50 + 56.2*0.68 = 88.2 degC; T_J,HS = 88.2 + 28.7*(0.80 + 0.41) = 122.9 degC; T_J,LS = 121.5 degC. Max R_DS(on): T_sink 92.8 degC, T_J,HS 131.1 degC. With screw-mounted pads (0.63 K/W): 118.1 / 125.7 degC. Nominal 400 V / 25 A: T_J,HS 112 degC. Switching loss +30 % (SKILL-006 principle 3 uncertainty): 129.7 degC. P_max per device (KR-TH-001) = (150 - 50)/(2*0.68 + 0.80 + 0.41) = 38.9 W against 28.7 W worst case (margin 1.36); the 125 degC preference gives 29.2 W, i.e. just met with typical parts and missed by 6 K with max-R_DS(on) parts. Upgrade LAM 5 D K 100 12 (0.3 K/W): T_J,HS 101.6 degC typ, 107.2 degC max R; P_max(125) = 41.4 W. In reality T_J settles lower because R_DS(on) at 115-125 degC is 8-12 % below the 150 degC value used here.

Fan failure: the natural-convection resistance of the single-width LAM 5 was not found; scaling the published 1.73 K/W of the double-width 125 mm unit by surface area gives roughly 3.5 K/W. Steady state would be T_sink = 50 + 56.2*3.5 = 247 degC (T_J > 280 degC); even the optimistic 1.73 K/W gives T_J,HS = 182 degC, above the 175 degC absolute maximum. The OTP therefore must act. With an estimated 0.25-0.30 kg aluminium mass, tau = m*c*R_nat = 790-950 s and the sink climbs from 88 to 100 degC in about 60-75 s, which the NTC trip catches; a fan tachometer fault should additionally force a derate within 2 s. Full-power operation without the fan is impossible, which the design-basis seed already implies.

The TI instance values quoted in SKILL-006 (CR201-50VE "0.5 degC/W", CD-02-05-247 "0.1 degC/W") are not reproducible: the Ohmite datasheet gives 3.3 K/W natural with no forced-air figure, and the Wakefield value is 0.107 degC-in2/W, an impedance per area. Neither was copied.

Selection: Sil-Pad TSP 3500, 0.254 mm, cut oversize (28 x 32 mm per device, or one 60 x 32 mm strip under both devices), no mounting hole, clip mounted. Reasons: best thermal impedance of the elastomer pads, 200 degC rating, 4 kVac breakdown (1.6x the 2.5 kV requirement and well above a 1.5 kVac / 2.1 kVdc basic-insulation type test at 480 V peak, to be confirmed by the isolation review), fibreglass carrier for cut-through resistance, and 3x lower coupling capacitance than the 76 um phase-change pad. The pad capacitance drives displacement current into protective earth at every edge (C*dv/dt = 47 pF * 50 V/ns = 2.3 A for ~10 ns); the thin ulTIMiFlux pad, although proven in TIDA-010054, would triple this and is kept only as a screw-mounted alternative. Al2O3 (29 pF) is the fallback if conducted CM emissions demand it, at the cost of grease on both faces and a larger-than-stock ceramic for creepage. Design value R_pad = 0.80 K/W (clip pressure about 25 psi; 40-60 N over 3.4 cm2 gives only 12-26 psi average) and 0.63 K/W for screw mounting at 50 psi; both are assumptions to be measured. Oversizing gives >= 5.5 mm of pad surface beyond every tab edge, so the creepage tab-to-sink is >= 5.5 mm, above the 5.0 mm I estimate for 500 V working voltage, pollution degree 2, material group IIIa (IEC 60664-1 Table F.5 from memory; KR-ISO-002 human review). Stock TO-247 die-cuts (24 x 19 mm) leave only 1.5-4 mm and are not acceptable here.

Hardware: clip mounting with the LAM 5 K retaining springs (spring force not published; verify >= 40 N) keeps the pad hole-free and places only the earthed clip against the plastic body (clip-to-lead clearance >= 3 mm to check). Screw alternative: Boyd 7721-7PPSG PPS shoulder washer (shoulder dia 3.43 mm fits the 3.6 mm tab hole, bore 2.95 mm -> #4-40 or M2.5 screw, not M3; 260 degC; torque 0.56-0.68 N m per distributor data) with a die-cut pad with hole; the 0.24 mm PPS wall is then the only solid insulation to the screw, which is why clips are preferred.

## 5. NTC placement and OTP mapping (KR-TH-003)

Sensor: Vishay NTCALUG01A103F ring-lug NTC (10 kohm +/-1 %, B25/85 3984 K, -40 to +150 degC, 23 mW/K, tau 7.5 s, 1500 Vac terminal-to-lug, AEC-Q200; datasheet 29092 rev 17-Nov-17), fixed with an M3 thread-forming screw on the device face of the sink between the two TO-247 bodies, <= 10 mm from the HS tab. The lug is at protective-earth potential; the control-side treatment (direct ADC input if the SELV control ground is bonded to PE, otherwise an isolated channel such as the LS driver AIN/APWM path of CB-PR-002) is an architecture decision surfaced below.

Readout: 2.2 kohm pull-up to a 3.00 V reference gives 2.46 V (25 degC), 0.98 V (85), 0.88 V (90), 0.71 V (100), 0.57 V (110), 0.41 V (125); sensitivity 15.5 mV/K = 21 LSB/K of the 12-bit ADC; self-heating 0.03 K. Mapping (not a measurement of T_J): T_J,HS ~ T_NTC + 4 K (sink spreading, assumed) + P_HS*(R_pad + R_JC) = T_NTC + 39 K at the worst corner (typ) and + 43 K (max R); at light load the offset collapses to a few kelvin, so firmware should estimate T_J = T_NTC + k*P_est(Vin, Iout) rather than add a fixed offset. Thresholds: warning/derate at 90 degC sink (T_J <= 133 degC), firmware trip at 100 degC (T_J <= 143 degC), hardware comparator into an ePWM trip zone at 110 degC as the last line (T_J about 150 degC at full-load losses). Worst-case steady-state sink temperature is 88-93 degC, so the 100 degC trip has 7-12 K margin; the chain must be calibrated with a resistor in place of the NTC (CB-PR-002 method) and validated with a thermocouple at the device footprint.

## 6. Copper temperature rise (KR-PCB-006, PE-PCB-006)

IPC-2221/2152-style estimate I = k * dT^0.44 * A^0.725 (k = 0.048 external, 0.024 internal; A in mil2) at 70 um (2.76 mil): 25 A / 10 K -> 12.7 mm external (33 mm internal); 25 A / 20 K -> 8.4 mm (21.7 mm); 27.5 A / 20 K -> 9.5 mm (24.8 mm). Rule: power nets >= 12 mm wide on outer layers (>= 22 mm on inner layers), repeated on two layers and stitched. Resistive loss at 100 degC: 12 mm x 70 um = 0.265 mohm/cm -> 0.17 W/cm at 25 A, about 2.5 W for a 15 cm total path (0.05 % efficiency). Layer transitions carrying 25 A need >= 24 vias of 0.3 mm drill (about 1 A each, conservative).

## 7. Other heat sources and distances

Inductor (6-10 W, 60-80 mm envelope assumed): natural convection with h = 8 W/m2K gives 20-58 K rise; in >= 2 m/s air (h = 25) 6-19 K. Place it laterally beside the sink in the fan bypass stream, >= 20 mm from the sink body and outside the exhaust. Exhaust air carries 56 W in 14-20 m3/h, i.e. +9 to +12 K above ambient (62 degC at 50 degC ambient). Film capacitors: hot-spot limits are typically 105 degC for MKP (to be confirmed from the capacitor agent's datasheets); design target <= 85 degC at 50 degC ambient, so >= 20 mm from the sink and out of the exhaust; electrolytics, if any, >= 30 mm. HV ceramics beside the bridge legs (KR-CAP-003) sit in the hottest PCB zone (lead copper at 90-100 degC) and must be rated >= 125 degC.

## 8. Mechanical envelope and PCB placement constraints

Reserve a 185 x 60 mm strip, 55 mm high: 100 mm body + 15 mm fan allowance + 30 mm intake + 30 mm exhaust clearance, plus 5 mm keep-out each side; exhaust toward an enclosure vent; no parts > 15 mm tall in the intake/exhaust zones. Both TO-247-4 on the long face toward the half-bridge area at 28 mm pitch, lead row 3-5 mm from the face, bodies 20-25 mm above the board; gate drivers and decoupling on the bottom side directly beneath the leads (SKILL-006 principle 4; KR-PCB-005; PE-PCB-001), so the thermal placement does not lengthen the commutation loop (KR-PCB-004, PE-PCB-003). No HV copper on outer layers within 5 mm of the sink outline and its earthed mounting pins; inner-layer HV pours under the sink only if the solid-insulation path is accepted (KR-ISO-002; slots per KR-ISO-004 where creepage limits). Sink bonded to PE by a dedicated pad; fan connector (12 V, GND, TACH) at the fan end; NTC leads as a twisted pair away from the switch node (PE-PCB-005). Mass about 0.25-0.35 kg (estimate) requires two to four M3 fixings in addition to the device clips. Partition compatibility: on a separate power board the sink, devices, pads, NTC and fan all stay on the power board; only the NTC and TACH signals cross to the control domain.

## 9. Limitations of the cooling assumptions

No CFD; lumped steady-state model with equal sharing (actual split 51/49 %); the 0.68 K/W figure is a distributor value at the fan's nominal flow for a uniformly heated profile, not two concentrated 28 W sources; interface resistance depends on clamp pressure (0.63-1.09 K/W over 10-50 psi); TI's factor 2 on the sink term is interpreted, not explained; 50 degC assumed at the fan intake with no enclosure preheating; radiation and PCB conduction neglected (conservative); the 10 s overload is treated as steady state (conservative, sink tau >> 10 s); natural-convection resistance of the LAM 5 is an estimate.
